title: WillowGrid hosted embeddings + rerank integration lab
summary: Intro demo of Redwood hosted embeddings + reranker endpoints. Walked through API calls, Console quickstarts, Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization. Customer concerns: latency vs cost, data retention, SSO and SOC2. Agreed next steps: pilot keys + sample dataset benchmark, security doc share, follow-up integration slot.
action_items: Marta Reyes - share hosted API quickstart snippet + example curl and Python - 2027-07-02
Jordan Liu - send security binder (SOC2 report, SSO guide, retention policy) - 2027-07-01
Priya Shah - provide 50 sample queries and 10k doc vectors for pilot - 2027-07-06
Ethan Cole - set up service account in staging and request pilot keys - 2027-07-02
next_steps: Redwood to provision short-lived pilot API key and demo dataset transform guide
Customer to run 50-query benchmark with supplied harness and share latency/cost numbers
Schedule follow-up technical check-in week of 2027-07-12
transcript:
Meeting started 14:00 UTC
00:00 Jordan Liu: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, Jordan from Redwood here, with Marta from our solutions team. Today we'll run a practical lab — hosted embeddings and the reranker flow, and show the Console and Optimize hints.
00:18 Priya Shah: Hi all, Priya here. We're mostly interested in improving site search relevance for product docs and support articles. Latency under 300ms would be ideal but cost is also a big constraint.
00:33 Jordan Liu: Great. Quick agenda: 1) show the embeddings API and vector size/encoding, 2) show retrieval + rerank endpoint pattern, 3) Console and Optimize suggestions, and 4) Q&A/security. Does that work?
00:45 Priya Shah: Yep.
00:48 Marta Reyes: I'll share my screen now — hope the deck pop's up, just a sec. (screen share noises) Ok, Console home.
01:10 Marta Reyes: On the left you can see Models -> Embeddings. We have precomputed profiles, and we expose the embedding endpoint as POST /v1/embeddings. You send text, get back float vectors. Example size: 1024 floats for the high-accuracy profile or 384 for the micro profile.
01:32 Samir Patel: Do you store vectors for hosted customers? How is retention handled?
01:38 Jordan Liu: Good question — hosted default is ephemeral by config; vectors can be stored in your own index. For Redwood-hosted indexing we have retention options and we can disable storage so only hash metadata is kept. We'll send the SOC2/retention doc after the call.
01:55 Ethan Cole: For the reranker, is that a separate endpoint or combined?
02:02 Marta Reyes: Both patterns exist. Typical flow: 1) retrieve top-K candidates from your vector DB (could be Pinecone or your own ES), 2) call Redwood /v1/rerank with the query, candidate snippets + embeddings if you want, and we return a score and optionally a re-ordered set. There's also a one-shot hybrid endpoint for small indices.
02:24 Priya Shah: Can you show the actual API payload?
02:28 Marta Reyes: Sure. (types) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' 
  -d '{"query":"how to reset password","candidates":[{"id":"a1","text":"To reset your password..."},...] }'
02:48 Jordan Liu: Note that passing candidate embeddings is optional — if you send them we avoid extra embed calls and it's cheaper. Passing the vector also lets us use a smaller reranker model that focuses on scoring.
03:03 Samir Patel: Are there size limits on candidate lists? We usually surface 100 candidates from our initial retrieval.
03:09 Marta Reyes: We recommend keeping reranker candidates under 200 for latency reasons. We have streaming responses for the reranker so you can early-fetch top results while the rest shuffle.
03:25 Ethan Cole: Streaming in what form? SSE or websockets?
03:29 Marta Reyes: SSE for the hosted API — chunked JSON events. Works well for browser clients or server-side streaming.
03:36 Priya Shah: Latency numbers — can you give ballpark for an end-to-end retrieval+rerank?
03:41 Jordan Liu: For embeddings at 384 dims + retrieval from your index + rerank of ~50 candidates, typical p50 is ~120–220ms depending on region. If you push 1024 dims and 200 candidates you might be 400–700ms. Batching, quantization and smaller reranker models reduce cost and latency — that's what Optimize recommends.
04:05 Samir Patel: Could you repeat the Optimize part?
04:09 Marta Reyes: Yes. Optimize inspects your query distribution and sequence lengths, then suggests batching windows, quantization profiles (e.g., int8 or 4-bit per-layer), and whether to use a smaller embedding profile for short queries. It also shows token-level cost breakdown in the Console.
04:28 Ethan Cole: We have compliance constraints — SSO with Okta, and our security team wants to know about KMS integration.
04:35 Jordan Liu: Redwood supports SAML/SSO via Okta and can integrate with your KMS for private deployments. For hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys using [KMS provider]. We'll include the KMS integration guide in the binder.
04:54 Priya Shah: Are there any multitenant isolation concerns if we do hosted? We prefer dedicated capacity if noisy neighbors are a risk.
05:03 Jordan Liu: Absolutely. Hosted is multi-tenant but isolated at the request level; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and stronger isolation. For high-SLA workloads we recommend dedicated. For a pilot it's common to start hosted with storage off.
05:20 Jordan Liu: Now I'll switch to a live demo with a small dataset. I'm going to run through creating embeddings for three docs.
05:30 Marta Reyes: (types) Running curl to embeddings endpoint - text payload - returns a vector. Copy/paste into local index.
06:00 Jordan Liu: Ok I'm going to call the rerank endpoint with a sample query — watch the Console network tab.
06:12 Jordan Liu: Sending request... got back streamed chunks, first chunk contains top-3; total time ~210ms from our region.
06:30 Priya Shah: Nice. Can the reranker return structured fields, like intent label or answer span?
06:36 Marta Reyes: Yes, you can ask for structured outputs — JSON with fields. It's similar to function-calling pattern, we return the label and score. The schema can be validated in the Console.
06:54 Samir Patel: How deterministic are scores across model versions? We need stable ordering for A/B tests.
07:01 Jordan Liu: We expose model versioning and you can pin a reranker model. Optimize will flag quality regressions when rolling models. There is some nondeterminism due to CPU/GPU discrepancies but for production we recommend pinning and running a small eval set to assert parity.
07:24 Ethan Cole: Does Redwood host evals or do we run them locally?
07:27 Marta Reyes: Both. Console has an Evals tab for running prompt sets; you can upload your test set and run against multiple models. We also provide the harness if you want to run local reproducible tests.
07:42 Priya Shah: Ok let's talk scale. We expect bursts to 100 QPS on search during peak. Can hosted handle that?
07:50 Jordan Liu: It depends on model choice and batching. For embedding-only throughput, smaller dims and batching give excellent throughput. For rerank at 100 QPS with 50 candidates, you'd likely need dedicated pools or a burst plan. We can run a quick capacity estimate during the pilot.
08:08 Samir Patel: What about costs? Any formula we can use to ballpark token/tokenized cost?
08:14 Marta Reyes: Console shows token-level cost. For embeds+rerank common pattern, cost = embed cost per doc (if you re-embed on ingest) + rerank cost per query which we show per-model. Optimize can simulate cost for your observed query distribution. We'll attach a sample spreadsheet.
08:33 Priya Shah: Can you do negative sampling / fine-tuning to improve rerank?
08:38 Marta Reyes: Instead of fine-tuning, many customers use prompt engineering on the reranker or a small supervised signal via Evals: provide labeled pairs and we suggest weighting and prompt templates. We also support fine-tuning in private deployments if you need model updates.
08:56 Jordan Liu: Quick pause for questions.
09:00 Ethan Cole: Integration question — our stack is Go + vector DB X. Any SDKs?
09:06 Marta Reyes: We have official Python and JS SDKs, and a simple REST API for Go. Also sample Go client in the docs. For vector DBs we show connectors for Pinecone, Milvus, and OpenSearch.
09:20 Samir Patel: What about retry/backoff guidance for the rerank endpoint?
09:24 Jordan Liu: Use idempotent retries for POST with request-id header and exponential backoff. We return helpful 429s with retry-after headers. Console traces show per-request headers and latency.
09:38 Priya Shah: For our pilot we'd like to try both flows: 1) host vectors in our DB + call rerank, 2) possible Redwood-hosted index to compare. Can you provision both test cases?
09:50 Jordan Liu: Yes, we can. We'll provide a step-by-step guide to ingest into your DB and to push to Redwood-hosted index with storage disabled/enabled.
10:02 Marta Reyes: Now showing Optimize tab. You can upload a small sample of queries and we auto-suggest batch sizes and model variants. See the 'cost delta' column — it predicts token and request cost.
10:18 Samir Patel: There's a note about quantization — is that transparent? Any change to accuracy?
10:25 Marta Reyes: Quantization like int8 or 4-bit can change outputs slightly. Optimize runs a small A/B on your sample set and reports quality delta. If regression is unacceptable you'll stick with higher-precision. Often for embeddings tiny deltas are tolerable and gain big cost wins.
10:44 Priya Shah: Our security team asked about audit logs for who called what — do you have token-level auditing?
10:50 Jordan Liu: Yes, Console has request-level logs and we can ship to your SIEM via webhook or S3. For Private deployments you can also plug into your audit pipeline. We'll include an example log export.
11:05 Ethan Cole: Any embargo or data residency constraints? We're EU-first for customer data.
11:11 Jordan Liu: We have EU regions; for data residency we can route to EU-only hosting and restrict embeddings regionally. For private deployments we can also run in your VPC.
11:25 Priya Shah: Walk me through a small benchmark plan — what should we measure?
11:29 Marta Reyes: Recommended: p50/p95 latency for embeddings and rerank separately, cost per 1k queries, and relevance metrics (MRR, MAP) on a labeled subset. Also measure memory/CPU on your retrieval node. We'll share a harness.
11:48 Samir Patel: Ok great. Is there any rate-limiting we should be aware of for the pilot keys?
11:53 Jordan Liu: Pilot keys have soft quotas; we'll set them to match your pilot needs. For production we set quotas and can show burst/scale policies.
12:05 Priya Shah: Could you demonstrate passing embeddings into the reranker to skip recomputation?
12:10 Marta Reyes: Yep — sending precomputed vectors reduces both latency and cost. I'm going to show a payload now where candidates include a base64-encoded vector.
12:26 Jordan Liu: You might see small numeric differences due to vector normalization; we suggest normalizing vectors client-side to L2=1.
12:33 Ethan Cole: Do you handle float32 arrays only? We use quantized storage in our DB.
12:39 Marta Reyes: We accept float arrays; if your DB stores int8/quantized formats you can decode client-side. Optimize can help by recommending a quantization profile that balances storage and accuracy.
12:54 Priya Shah: About the reranker model size — can we choose a tiny model for faster scoring?
12:58 Jordan Liu: Yes, there are model tiers: micro, standard, and high-accuracy. Micro is optimized for speed/cost; standard gives a good balance. Optimize will propose the model tier based on your eval set.
13:15 Samir Patel: Any tips for candidate selection heuristics?
13:18 Marta Reyes: Combine sparse signals (BM25) and dense retrieval and then rerank. For ambiguous queries upweight recency or click telemetry. Also consider a confidence threshold to fall back to simple retrieval for latency-sensitive queries.
13:35 Priya Shah: Could you show the Console's trace for a mixed flow?
13:40 Marta Reyes: Switching to Traces. Here's a sample trace showing retrieval time, embed call time, rerank streaming chunks and final aggregation. It highlights the percent of time spent in each stage.
13:58 Ethan Cole: If we do canary model rollouts, will user traffic be split at the request level?
14:03 Jordan Liu: Yes, route rules allow Canary -> 10% traffic to new model, 90% to control. We can auto-roll back on quality regressions.
14:12 Priya Shah: How are regressions detected? Do you rely on labeled sets only?
14:16 Marta Reyes: You can use labeled sets plus synthetic probes and live user feedback. Optimize supports thresholds for auto-alerts on MRR or other metrics.
14:30 (short silence)
14:35 Jordan Liu: Quick demo of an automated suggestion — Optimize just recommended switching to a 384 embed and micro reranker for 30% cost savings on this sample set with under 2% MRR drop.
14:51 Samir Patel: That seems promising. We'll want to validate on our domain.
14:56 Priya Shah: Ok anything else on integrations?
15:00 Ethan Cole: One more — do you expose a client-side SDK to compute embeddings in Rust? We have Rust services.
15:07 Marta Reyes: Not officially, but the REST API works fine and community customers have small Rust clients. We can add a sample repo link.
15:18 Jordan Liu: Alright, let's recap next steps. We'll provision pilot keys, share the security binder and the sample harness, and Marta will send quickstart snippets.
15:29 Priya Shah: Sounds good. Thanks, this was helpful.
15:32 Jordan Liu: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with dates for the tech check-in.
15:38 -- END OF CALL --
notes: Customer curious about switching to micro models and quantization to save cost; security questions around SSO/KMS; agreed pilot with sample queries and two integration modes (hosted index vs client index).
extra_metadata: pilot plan includes two scenarios: client-hosted vectors + Redwood rerank, and Redwood-hosted index with storage disabled
sample harness will include a JMeter script for concurrency testing
